items.title: Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas advises Ethereal Exploration Guild on acquisition of industrial land in Tirupati
items.summary: Ethereal Exploration Guild Private Limited has entered into an agreement with the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation Limited for an industrial land parcel admeasuring 142.3 acres, situated in Routhsuramala Village, Tirupati District, Andhra Pradesh. Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas & Co advised Ethereal Exploration Guild on this land acquisition deal. The Firm was involved in the review of revenue documents, and the negotiation and finalisation of the agreement for sale with APIIC. The Firm also advised Ethereal in relation to various other aspects of the transaction. The transaction team consisted of Mrinal Kumar (Partner), Arnav Sahni (Partner), and Aman Gupta (Senior Associate). Ethereal intends to utilise the land to establish a large-scale, integrated manufacturing and testing facility for rocket engines and launch vehicles, with a proposed investment of approximately ₹578.39 crore. items.title: Madras High Court bars videos linked to POCSO case against GEM Granites founder R Veeramani
items.summary: The Madras High Court on Friday restrained media organisations, intermediaries and digital platforms from publishing or circulating videos linked to the ongoing investigation against GEM Granites founder R Veeramani in connection with a case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act) [Tulir Charitable Trust Vs Commissioner] Justice V Lakshminarayanan passed the interim order after observing that publication of video material connected with the investigation could reveal the identities of the victims and discourage other victims from coming forward and recording their statements before the police. The Court noted that the investigation was at an advanced and crucial stage and that the police were still trying to ascertain whether there were more victims than those already identified. “ At this juncture, if there were to be news debates or photographs being uploaded, there is a distinct possibility that other victims might not come forward to record their statement to the police, fearing the consequences it can have on their lives, ” the Court said. items.title: Four-member all-woman SIT formed to probe Veeramani POCSO case
items.summary: The Tamil Nadu Police on Thursday, September 24, formed a four-member all-woman Special Investigation Team (SIT) to investigate the child sexual assault case and related allegations against Gem Group of Companies chairman R Veeramani, amid scrutiny of the handling of the earlier probe. Director-General of Police Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal ordered the formation of the SIT, which will be headed by Additional Commissioner of Police PC Thenmozhi of the Central Crime Branch. Joint Commissioner Disha Mittal, Superintendent of Police J Mutharasi, and Superintendent of Police VV Geethanjali are the other members. The formation of the SIT came on the same day that action was taken against three police officers involved in the earlier probe. Additional Director General of Police A Arun and Inspector General of Police/Commissioner of Police, Coimbatore City N Kannan were placed under compulsory wait at the office of the DGP. Assistant Commissioner MA Yasmin of the Koyambedu Range was transferred to the Chief Office Vacancy Reserve on administrative grounds. Delhi High Court denies anticipatory bail to Ajeet Bharti in SC/ST Act case
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday denied anticipatory bail to YouTuber Ajeet Bharti in the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (SC/ST Act) case registered against him for his comments regarding Member of Parliament (MP) Chandrashekhar Azad Ravan. Justice Saurabh Banerjee said that the offence under Sections 3(1)(r) and 3(1)(s) of the ST/ST Act was prima facie made out against Bharti and that there was a statutory bar on granting anticipatory bail. Section 3(1)(r) deals with intentional insult or intimidation with intent to humiliate members of the SC/ST community. Section 3(1)(s) relates to abusing any member of the SC/ST community by caste name. The Court added that the petition was not maintainable and therefore was being dismissed. A detailed order is awaited. Justice Saurabh Banerjee Bharti had challenged the trial court's order of September 7 that denied him the relief of anticipatory bail. A first information report (FIR) was registered against him at Delhi's North Avenue Police Station on August 23 under the SC/ST Act, along with Section 67 of the IT Act and Sections 196(1)(c) and 351(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. items.title: Delhi High Court asks Centre to decide SFI's plea against Instagram  account blocking
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday asked the Central government's grievance appellate committee (GAC) to decide the Students' Federation of India (SFI) appeal against the blocking of its Instagram account. Justice Amit Mahajan said that he expects the SFI's appeal to be decided in three weeks. SFI is the student wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist). The court passed the order on a plea filed by SFI. Advocate Apar Gupta appeared for the student organisation and stated the statutory time period prescribed to decide such an appeal is four weeks. He said the Court had previously disposed off similar matters with direction to the government to decide the appeal in an additional four weeks. The Court recorded that the SFI had filed the appeal before the government on August 12 and no order has been passed till date. It then disposed of the plea, asking the government to decide the appeal. According to SFI, Instagram permanently disabled the SFI Delhi account on July 5, stating that it “may be associated with another account that has gone against our rules” and therefore did not comply with its community standards on account integrity. items.title: Supreme Court gives Centre last chance to explain steps taken against child porn online
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday gave the Central government one last opportunity to explain what it has done to curb the circulation of child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) on social media platforms [ Just Rights for Children Alliance & Anr. v. S. Harish & Ors. ]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran passed the direction while hearing a plea filed by the Just Rights for Children Alliance (JRCA), seeking criminal action against intermediaries that fail to report CSEAM. The Court noted that the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and the Ministry of Law and Justice had yet to file the response it sought on August 14. “ Unfortunately, till this date, no such counter or report has come on record. The matter before us is extremely serious. We grant one last opportunity to both the ministries to file that counter/report, ” the Court said. items.title: Judicial process must provide remedy, not merely identify litigant's wound: Madras High Court
items.summary: The judicial process is meant not merely to identify a litigant’s “wound” but also to provide a remedy for it, the Madras High Court recently observed. [Muthulakshmi v. Raju] A Division Bench of Justices N Anand Venkatesh and KK Ramakrishnan said that courts must keep in mind the human dimension of litigation and ensure that procedural law does not become a means to postpone, dilute or ultimately deny substantive justice. "The judicial process is intended not merely to identify the existence of a wound but also to provide the legally permissible remedy for its redressal." The Bench added that courts exist to render substantive justice and that procedural complexities cannot be allowed to defeat lawful rights. Justices Anand Venkatesh and KK Ramakrishnan The Court was dealing with a commercial appeal arising from a prolonged partnership dispute in which the litigant had moved through multiple civil and arbitration proceedings without her substantive claims being adjudicated on merits. items.title: P&H High Court cancels murder accused's bail after his 'band baja dunga' threat
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has cancelled the bail granted to a murder accused after he sent various threatening messages to the complainant and his family, including one saying "band baja dunga" [Sourabh Narula v State of Haryana & Anr] Justice Vikram Aggarwal said the accused cannot be permitted to remain on bail because any untoward incident can take place if he is allowed to remain free. "In the considered opinion of this Court, he has violated the most essential condition of the order granting bail by threatening the complainant side," the Court said. Justice Vikram Aggarwal The accused Suresh alias Binni Sardana is accused of having committed the murder of one Shyam Lal, who was the servant of one Mukul, a cousin of the complainant Sourabh Narula. Suresh was granted bail on January 28 by the High Court in the case dating back to June 24, 2023. However, soon after he came out of the prison, the accused allegedly started threatening the accused. Narula then moved the Court. In his petition, the complainant said that he and his father received threatening messages on Instagram and Facebook from the accused. One message to the complainant's sister was flagged in particular.

items.title: Supreme Court reserves verdict on plea challenging survey of Sambhal mosque
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday reserved its verdict on a plea filed by the Shahi Jama Masjid Committee at Sambhal challenging a trial court order directing the appointment of an Advocate Commissioner to survey the mosque's premises [ Committee Management, Jami Masjid Sambhal v. Hari Shankar Jain & Ors. ]. A Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe reserved its decision on the plea challenging the Allahabad High Court's May 2025 decision to uphold the trial court's ex-parte order allowing the survey of the mosque's premises. Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe The trial court had passed its November 2024 directive in a suit involving allegations that the mosque was constructed over a demolished Hindu temple during the Mughal era. The suit was filed by advocate Hari Shankar Jain and seven others. The civil court order allowing the survey had led to violent clashes in Sambhal. items.title: Supreme Court seeks NIA response to bail plea of man accused of links to Dawood Ibrahim’s gang
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday issued notice on a bail plea filed by a man accused of helping the gang led by terrorist Dawood Ibrahim extort money and move funds through hawala routes [ Shabbir Abubakar Shaikh v. National Investigation Agency ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta sought the National Investigation Agency’s (NIA) response to a plea filed by Shabbir Abubakar Shaikh challenging a Bombay High Court order that refused him bail. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta The NIA alleges that Shaikh acted on instructions from Dawood Ibrahim and Chhota Shakeel and helped extort ₹16 crores from a protected witness between 2008 and 2018. It also claims he received ₹25 lakhs through hawala routes in April 2022, kept ₹5 lakhs and passed the remaining ₹20 lakhs to another accused. The agency alleges that the money was intended for terrorist and criminal activities. Shaikh disputes his alleged links to the gang and denies that the money was meant for terrorism. He has also challenged the application of the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act, 1999 (MCOCA) to his case. A special NIA court rejected his bail plea in December 2024. items.title: Air India fined ₹50k for de-boarding disabled woman, damaging wheelchair
items.summary: The Court of the Chief Commissioner for Persons With Disabilities (CCPD court) recently imposed a ₹50,000 fine on Air India for regulatory violations, apart from recommending that it pay ₹5 lakhs as compensation to a disabled woman for de-boarding her from the plane without reasons. The order was passed on September 24 by the Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities S Govindaraj on a complaint by Falguni Maheshwari. Maheshwari, a wheelchair-bound woman with 80 percent locomotor disability, flew from Frankfurt to India in May 2026 on an Air India flight. However, she was de-boarded from a connecting flight that was to take her from Delhi to Bhuj without providing any written reasons. The complainant also alleged that her wheelchair was returned in a damaged condition. She stated that she was forced to arrange alternative flights at her own expense under severe emotional distress. Air India stated that de-planing the woman regulatory necessity solely on safety grounds. It stated that at the time of boarding, the woman was displaying certain medical concerns. items.title: Kerala High Court reserves verdict on ex-DGP Tomin Thachankery's plea to suspend jail sentence
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Thursday reserved its verdict on a plea by former Director General of Police (DGP) Tomin Thachankary for the suspension of his 4-year jail sentence in a disproportionate assets case [ Tomin J Thachakary v. State of Kerala ]. Thachankary has sought a suspension of his jail sentence until his appeal against the trial court's conviction and sentence against him is decided by the High Court. Justice A Badharudeen today reserved his verdict on this question of interim relief. Notably, the judge also observed that the grant of such interim relief, in some cases, becomes disproportionately favourable to the accused. A conviction in corruption cases itself is an uphill task, the judge pointed out. "What is happening here is, getting a conviction or a trial itself is a difficult task. Trial will be stalled in multiple ways. Ultimately, even after conviction and sentence, they will easily get released by appellate powers. Then they continue outside without even hearing the appeal. items.title: Kerala High Court directs State Bar Council to identify advocates who haven't cleared AIBE since 2021
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Wednesday issued directions to the Bar Council of Kerala (BCK) to identify and publish names of advocates who have not qualified the All India Bar Examination (AIBE) from 2021 onwards. [Amarnath Joshi Surendiran v The Secretary, Bar Council of Kerala & ors] A Division Bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice Syam Kumar VM directed the Kerala Bar Council to complete the exercise within 8 weeks. The Bench passed the directions after considering an affidavit filed by the Council detailing the steps it had been taken as per the Court's earlier order dated August 19 . In that order, the Court had specifically directed the Council to publish the names of 1,157 advocates who were enrolled between 2010 and 2021, but had not cleared the AIBE. It had also directed court registries not to register matters in which any of these advocates had filed vakalatnamas and ordered that the list is forwarded to district courts across Kerala. Considering the possibility of similar instances arising in the future and cases that may have arisen after 2021, the Court directed the Council to update its records. items.title: Supreme Court seeks progress reports from High Courts on 8 lakh pending civil execution petitions
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday observed that merely seeking pendency figures every 6 months is insufficient to tackle the backlog of civil execution petitions, which currently stands at over 8 lakh cases across district courts nationwide [Periyammal (Dead) and Ors. vs V Rajamani and Anr.]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran took up the matter to review compliance reports submitted by various High Courts following its earlier directives on curbing execution delays. The proceedings stem from a ruling passed on March 6, 2025 , where the top court resolved a four-decade-old property dispute from 1986. Holding that delay frustrates a decree-holder’s right to reap the fruits of a decree, the Court directed all High Courts to mandate that lower courts decide execution petitions within 6 months, failing which, presiding judicial officers would be held administratively answerable. Senior Advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan , appearing as Amicus Curiae , placed a compilation before the Bench, pointing out that High Courts attributed delays to interim stays, objection petitions, counsel non-appearance and frequent adjournments.
